name: Unlearning
description: Headphone music for unlearning: for anyone loosening the grip of a high-control belief system, a rigid upbringing or an old certainty, and finding their own voice again. A hymn that spreads from a point in your head into open space, slogans whispered from every side that fade one by one, an insistent voice and your own trading ears, a unison that drifts apart into two views, a march that fades while your own rhythm grows, questions left unresolved, a tune that exists only between your two ears, and rest over slow binaural drones before a first morning. Each sketch is a short piece with its own sections that plays once, slows and comes to rest, and each explains its trick in the comments. This is music, not therapy: if leaving has been hard, be gentle with yourself and lean on people you trust. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Loosening the Hymn
sketches.description: The hymn you were taught, four square chords on the organ, steps through the interaural phase: it starts in the centre of your head and spreads into a haze around you. From the fifth bar a line of your own enters and stays, through to a slow amen that comes home to C. On speakers the 180-degree bars of the organ nearly vanish. Plays once, just under two minutes.

sketches.name: Echo Chamber
sketches.description: Headphones on: the same few words are whispered from every side of your head at once, then each voice fades away in turn, until only a still pad in the middle and your own breathing remain. Plays once from the start, about a minute and a half, and slows into stillness.

sketches.name: Two Voices
sketches.description: An old, insistent voice leans into one ear and your own voice into the other, through a level difference between the ears. Every fourth bar they trade places, so neither owns either ear, and over time the old voice grows quieter. In the last section it is gone, and your voice sits in the middle of your head. Plays once, about two minutes.

sketches.name: Cents of Doubt
sketches.description: One certainty, sounded in perfect unison, slowly drifts apart between the ears in cents and comes back again: at 3 cents it beats slowly, at 8 and 15 it shimmers, and at 30 it opens into a chorus of two views. Then it begins to drift a second time, and the piece slows to a stop while the two views are still apart. A piano asks and answers in the centre. Plays once, about two minutes.

sketches.name: Your Own Rhythm
sketches.description: The march you kept step to plays dead centre, square and loud, and fades away from the fourth bar, while your own rhythm grows from nothing: hand drums placed all around you and a kalimba swaying between your ears on delays under a millisecond. It settles on a held low C and stops. Plays once, about a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Turning It Over
sketches.description: A drone's phase turns slowly between your ears, so it rolls around inside your head like an idea being turned over. Four bars of questions in the whole-tone scale, which has no home note, are followed by four bars of an answer in lydian that is allowed to stay open. The questions come back faster, the answer once more, and the piece ends on an open chord. All rates stay below 3 Hz. Plays once, about a minute and a half.
sketches.source:
setcpm(56/4)

// The whole piece, played once: question, answer, the question again (faster), the answer, then open
song("question@4 answer@4 question'@4 answer'@4 open@4", "once")
tempomap("0:14 16:14 20:10")

// irate turns the phase between the ears, in turns per second: an idea rolled over slowly
// All rates stay below 3 Hz, so no pulse warning is needed
drone: note("[e2,b2]").s("sine").irate("<.2 .2 .4 .4 .8 .8 .4 .4>")
  .attack(1).sustain(1).release(1).gain(.24)

// Questions in the whole-tone scale, which has no home note
// variant: the second time, the questions come twice as fast
questions: n("<[0 1 2 3] [4@3 3] [2 3 4 5] [6@4]>").scale("E:whole tone").transpose(12)
  .sections("question").variant(x => x.ply(2))
  .s("sine").timbre("hollow").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.12)
  .attack(.08).sustain(.6).release(.8).room(.6).gain(.22)

// An answer in lydian that is allowed to stay open
answers: n("<[0 1 2 4] [5@3 4] [3 2 1 2] [4@4]>").scale("E:lydian").transpose(12)
  .sections("answer")
  .s("sine").timbre("hollow").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.12)
  .attack(.08).sustain(.6).release(.8).room(.6).gain(.22)

// A pad that follows the same sections: an augmented chord for the questions, open chords for the answer
qpad: note("[e3,g#3,c4]").sections("question")
  .s("sawtooth").unison(3).detune(.2).lpf(1200)
  .attack(1.5).sustain(.9).release(2).room(.6).gain(.1)
apad: note("<[e3,g#3,b3] [a2,c#3,e3,g#3]>").slow(2).sections("answer open")
  .s("sawtooth").unison(3).detune(.2).lpf(1200)
  .attack(1.5).sustain(.9).release(2).room(.6).gain(.1)

sketches.name: A Voice Only You Can Hear
sketches.description: Each ear alone hears only a hiss of white noise; together they carry a faint tune between them (Huggins pitch), something nobody can hand you, only hear for yourself. For the first sixteen bars a quiet sine plays the first phrase every four bars so you know what to listen for; for the last eight you listen alone. The effect is faint and differs between listeners. Plays once, about a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Wide Open
sketches.description: Headphones on: soft noise steps from identical in both ears, a narrow point in the middle of your head, to unrelated in each, wide and all around you, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning. A bell marks each step outward; then the space stays open and the piece slows to rest on G minor. Plays once, about two minutes.

sketches.name: Theta Integration
sketches.description: Headphones on: a 6 Hz binaural beat in the theta range under slow choir chords. For the first eight bars a pad sends alternate partials to each ear, so it sounds whole only when both ears hear it together; for the last eight the pieces have come back into one and each ear hears it whole. A stream runs nearby. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse. Plays once, about a minute and a half.

sketches.name: First Morning
sketches.description: The first morning after: at dawn only birds, placed all around you, with a lark gliding high overhead; then a flute and harp straight ahead, a wide breeze through an open door and a quiet 10 Hz binaural beat in the alpha range for waking gently. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse. Plays once, about a minute and a half.
sketches.source:
setcpm(80/4)

// The whole piece, played once: dawn with only the birds, then the morning
song("dawn@4 morning@28", "once")
tempomap("0:20 28:20 32:16")

// The first morning: birds placed all around you, each in its own place
robin: s("bird").slow(2).azimuth(-40).distance(3).gain(.22)
wren: s("bird").slow(3).azimuth(60).elevation(25).distance(4).gain(.18)
lark: s("bird").slow(4).azimuth(saw.range(-90, 90).slow(16)).elevation(50).distance(8).posglide(.5).gain(.14)

// A 10 Hz binaural beat in the alpha range: keep it quiet
drone: note("<g2 g2 e2 c2>").slow(2).s("sine").binaural(10)
  .attack(3).sustain(1).release(4).gain(.12)

// A flute straight ahead, the same in both ears, and a harp: G, Em, C, D
// Both wait for the morning; the flute restarts its phrase at the start of the section
flute: note("<[d5@2 b4 g4 b4@2 d5@2] [e5@3 d5 b4@4] [c5@2 e5 g5 e5@2 d5 c5] [d5@6 ~@2]>")
  .s("sine").timbre("hollow").vib(5).vibdepth(.1)
  .attack(.06).sustain(.6).release(.5).delay(.25).delaytime(3/8).room(.5).gain(.22)
  .sections("morning")
harp: note("<[g3 b3 d4 b3] [e3 g3 b3 g3] [c4 e4 g4 e4] [d3 f#3 a3 f#3]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("soft").decay(.4).sustain(0).release(.5).room(.5).gain(.18)
  .sections("morning")

// The door is open: the breeze comes in wide, unrelated in each ear
breeze: s("pink").slow(8).icorr(.15).hpf(300).lpf(2000).gain(.025)
